A real photograph, a still frame from a live-action commercial shot on a large-format 65mm digital cinema camera. EXACTLY TWO PEOPLE in frame, and no one else on the street.

A close two-shot on a city sidewalk. The two friends fill the lower centre and right of the frame, about 1.5 metres from camera, holding each other in a tight hug, cheek to cheek, and both faces turned toward camera. On the left is a white city bus, parked at the kerb about 4 metres away, its long row of dark tinted windows receding toward the frame edge. Behind the bus is the pale concrete side of a mid-rise building. The sidewalk and street run straight back into depth, with a white delivery van parked about 40 metres down the street and a row of small round street trees shrinking into the distance under an open sky.

Seen from just above shoulder height, close in. 35mm lens, natural perspective, straight lines, both faces sharp, the bus slightly soft and the far street clearly out of focus.

The woman on the left is the one in the first reference: same face, long dark hair in a single braid over her shoulder, light-wash denim jacket, white T-shirt and black jeans. The man on the right is the one in the second reference: same face, short swept blond hair, olive bomber jacket, khaki chinos. Her right arm is around his back and her right hand lies flat on his shoulder blade, with all five fingers visible. His left arm wraps around her shoulders and his left hand holds her upper arm. Every hand belongs to an arm you can follow back to a shoulder. No hand is loose or floating.

The sidewalk is grey concrete slabs with expansion joints, gum spots and a darker damp patch by the kerb. The bus has road grime along the lower panels, scuffed rubber at the door seals and reflections of the street in its windows. The building has rain streaks under its window ledges and a dented steel downpipe. Thin cracked kerb stones run along the gutter.

Light: late morning sun from high camera right, behind the bus line, giving both faces a soft side light. The far side of the street is in bright sun, and the shadow side of the bus and building falls off to cool, readable shade. The sky is pale blue, brighter at the horizon. Exposed for their faces.

Tactile realism: rich blacks with readable colour, soft highlight roll-off, truthful skin colour, restrained fine grain over a sharp image. Texture comes from real surfaces and light, never a filter. Any signs, the bus destination display or screens have no readable letters.

If any surface looks clean, plastic, grey, untextured or rendered, the image is wrong.
